Predict topics or timestamps for new documents

Source: R/methods.R
predict.tot.Rd

Runs Gibbs sampling on new documents with the fitted topic-word and topic-time distributions held fixed ("fold-in").

Usage

# S3 method for class 'tot'
predict(
  object,
  newdata,
  type = c("topics", "time"),
  time = NULL,
  n_iter = 100L,
  n_grid = 512L,
  ...
)

Arguments

object

A fitted "tot" model.

newdata

A document-term matrix (see tot()). Columns are matched to the training vocabulary by name when both have column names; unknown words are dropped. Without names, columns must be in training order.

type

"topics" for document-topic proportions, or "time" for predicted timestamps.

time

Optional timestamps of newdata, used by type = "topics" so that time also informs the topic assignments.

n_iter

Number of fold-in sweeps.

n_grid

Number of grid points for type = "time".

...

Unused.

Value

For type = "topics", a documents x topics matrix whose rows sum to 1. For type = "time", a vector of timestamps on the scale of the training time (NA for documents without known words).

Details

With type = "time", topics are sampled from the words alone and the timestamp is chosen to maximize \(\sum_i \log p(t \mid \psi_{z_i})\) over a grid spanning the training time range, as in Section 2 of Wang and McCallum (2006).

Examples

set.seed(1)
sim <- simulate_tot(n_docs = 100, n_topics = 3)
fit <- tot(sim$x, sim$time, k = 3, n_iter = 50)
head(predict(fit, sim$x[1:5, ], type = "topics"))
#>         Topic1    Topic2    Topic3
#> doc1 0.1766667 0.3266667 0.4966667
#> doc2 0.2466667 0.5166667 0.2366667
#> doc3 0.6366667 0.1866667 0.1766667
#> doc4 0.1766667 0.2766667 0.5466667
#> doc5 0.6166667 0.2066667 0.1766667
predict(fit, sim$x[1:5, ], type = "time")
#>      doc1      doc2      doc3      doc4      doc5 
#> 0.2622810 0.4177979 0.8037796 0.1835857 0.8300114
